Non-Use Cancellation in China: How to Build a Use-Evidence File Before CNIPA Acts

From 1 January 2027, a Chinese registration can be cancelled not only on a third party's request but on the authority's own initiative. That makes a use-evidence file a day-one operational task.

What Changes on 1 January 2027

Article 57 of the 2026 Trademark Law keeps the familiar rule: a registered mark that has become the generic name of its goods, or that has not been used for three consecutive years without justified reason, may be cancelled on the application of any party. It then adds a third paragraph: where those circumstances exist, the trademark authority may cancel the registration on its own initiative.

Two related changes raise the stakes. Article 2 expressly includes use through the internet and information networks within the definition of trademark use, giving dated e-commerce and social records a clearer role. Article 78 provides that where the rights holder has not used the mark in the preceding three years, an accused infringer may not be liable for damages — idle registrations lose practical enforceability even before they are cancelled.

The authority must decide a cancellation application within nine months, extendable by three (Art. 57). A party dissatisfied with the decision may request review within 15 days (Art. 58).

One Rule, Two Directions

Offensive useDefensive exposure
Who is at riskA squatter or blocker who registered a mark but never traded under itA legitimate foreign brand with dormant defensive registrations in classes it does not currently sell in
Typical actionFile a non-use cancellation to clear a blocking mark, often alongside an invalidation or a negotiated purchaseRespond to a cancellation notice or a proactive review with a dated evidence file
What winsShowing the opponent has no genuine commercial useProducing a continuous, dated chain of real use on the registered goods
New in 2027The authority can act without a private applicantNo private trigger is needed for a dormant mark to be examined

The same reform is therefore both a cheaper way to remove squatters and a reason to audit your own portfolio. Compare all recovery routes in What Happens If Someone Registers Your Trademark First.

The Five Official Requirements for Valid Use Evidence

CNIPA's Trademark Office FAQ on electronic filings sets out what evidence must show. All five need to be satisfied:

  1. The mark itself — the evidence must display the registered sign as used.
  2. The designated goods or services — use must be on the goods/services for which the mark is registered, not merely in an adjacent class.
  3. The user — the registrant, or a licensee; where a licensee used the mark, the licence relationship must itself be provable.
  4. The date — within the three years counted backwards from the date the cancellation application was filed, not from the registration date.
  5. The territory — use within the territorial scope of the PRC Trademark Law. Overseas sales alone are not enough.

The same FAQ lists acceptable forms: sales contracts and service agreements with their corresponding invoices, inspection reports, import/export declarations and comparable transaction documents. It also states that registration information, basic company information and awards generally do not count as use evidence.

What to Archive — and What Not to Rely On

Strong evidenceCommonly rejected
Dated sales contracts with matching VAT invoices and payment recordsUndated self-produced brochures
Import/export declarations, logistics and inspection reportsHandwritten receipts or contracts without a company seal
Packaging, labels and product photos showing the mark on the goodsTrademark registration certificates and company profiles
E-commerce listings with capture dates, order records and platform back-end reportsSocial posts or private-chat screenshots with no third-party corroboration
Advertising insertion orders, media placements, trade-fair photos with datesSymbolic or token use made only to defend a cancellation
Licence agreements plus the licensee's sales documentsUse of a materially different sign, or use on non-designated goods

CNIPA guidance and practitioner commentary consistently emphasise real, public, lawful use in the course of trade that reaches the market. A defensible alternative, where use genuinely did not occur, is to prove justified reasons — typically force majeure, government policy restrictions or bankruptcy liquidation. Lack of budget or poor sales are not accepted as justification.

A Quarterly Archiving SOP

  1. Index by mark and by class, not by business unit. A single word mark registered in six classes needs six evidence folders.
  2. File English and Chinese marks separately. They are separate rights in China and need separate evidence chains.
  3. Capture the date at source. Screenshots need a visible capture date; contracts and invoices need the counterparty, the SKU and the mark printed on them.
  4. Keep the licence chain. If a distributor or licensee produces the evidence, keep the licence agreement and recordal documents beside it.
  5. Quarterly review, rolling three-year window. Anything older than three years should be retained but flagged as no longer protective.
  6. Store immutably. A shared drive with version history, timestamps or notarised copies is easier to defend than a folder assembled after a notice arrives.

Tie this to renewal and monitoring: the same folder supports opposition evidence, enforcement complaints and renewal decisions. See our monitoring guide.

If a Cancellation Notice Arrives

ItemRule
Reply deadline2 months from receipt of the notice to submit use evidence or explain justified non-use (CNIPA FAQ / Implementing Regulations)
Electronic vs paperOnce you choose electronic submission of use evidence, subsequent documents are served electronically and further paper evidence is not accepted
One application, one classA single non-use cancellation application can only target one class, even for a multi-class registration
Review15 days to request review of a cancellation decision; review decided within 9 months, extendable by 3 (Art. 58)

Because the reply window is short and the evidence must pre-date the application, the work is almost entirely done before the notice exists. That is the argument for treating archiving as a routine control rather than a legal project.

Sources and Caveats

Primary sources: Articles 2, 57, 58 and 78 of the Trademark Law of the PRC (2026 Revision) (CNIPA, 26 June 2026); CNIPA Trademark Office, FAQ on Electronic Applications for Opposition, Non-Use Cancellation and Invalidation; CNIPA public reply on evidence for non-use cancellation; CNIPA Main Contents of the Revision (10 July 2026). Procedures and evidence practice may be refined by the revised Implementing Regulations and Examination Guidelines. This is general information, not legal advice.
